text:
claire: quick heads-up — onboarding logs for the go and python samples are leaking request ids into structured logs when OTEL_AUTO is enabled in the image. noticed during user testing video prep.

jon: thanks, which builds?

claire: onboarding image redwood/samples:onboard-2026-03 has OTEL_AUTO=true by default now. repro: `docker run -e OTEL_AUTO=true redwood/samples:onboard-2026-03` then `curl -H 'x-request-id: clz_abcdef123456' localhost:8080/generate`. The json logger field `req_id` is unredacted.

pepper: repro'd. JSON example (redacted manually):
```
{"level":"info","ts":"2026-03-24T11:02:03Z","msg":"recv","req_id":"clz_abcdef123456","user":"sam@example.com"}
{"level":"debug","ts":"2026-03-24T11:02:03Z","otel":"tracing","trace_id":"a1b2c3..."}
{"level":"info","ts":"2026-03-24T11:02:03Z","msg":"dispatch","req_id":"clz_abcdef123456","route":"/generate"}
```
claire: JSON logs are ingested by cloud logging and show up in the onboarding demos. Having raw ids there is a privacy problem.

jon: looks like the instrumentation in Go injects context earlier than our redact middleware. Node sample had the redaction working because middleware order was different. This is an SDK parity issue across languages.

pepper: also observed that stdout-scrubber shell trick breaks JSON escaping for some logs, so that's not safe for structured logs.

claire: immediate mitigations I propose: 1) flip onboarding image default to OTEL_AUTO=false until we have parity, 2) add a CI assertion in samples repo that after a request the captured logs contain no `clz_[0-9a-f]{6,}` patterns at INFO level, 3) add `redwood.telemetry.sensitive_fields` config to SDKs so apps can list fields (e.g., ["req_id","user_email"]) to be scrubbed from structured log payloads.

jon: agree on the flip for images. For longer term: SDK should offer a post-instrumentation hook that receives the final log payload so SDK or app can run redactors before emission. API sketch for Go: `telemetry.SetPostEmitHook(func(level string, payload map[string]interface{}) map[string]interface{})` — but we need to avoid nested types in our cross-language RFC.

pepper: from QA POV add an e2e test for onboarding that toggles OTEL_AUTO and asserts both plain text and JSON streams are clean. I'll open a test ticket.

qa-bot: created ticket SAMPLES-490: "structured log redaction + OTEL parity" and linked PR draft https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/230 (flip OTEL_AUTO)

devex-bot: draft docs note created https://go/redev/telemetry-structured-redact (internal draft) with checklist and recommended SDK config keys.

claire: one gotcha: some libraries add `request_id` under different field names (`req_id`, `requestId`, `x_request_id`). Redactor needs normalization. Suggest `sensitive_fields` matchers are case-insensitive and support dash/underscore variants.

jon: good call. Also propose adding a default redaction rule set shipped with SDKs for common header names and `clz_` pattern. That buys time while customers upgrade.

pepper: tagging @docs for onboarding video edits. We'll postpone publishing until images are flipped.

claire: PR incoming for image flip and adding CI log assertion. Will file SDK RFC for post-emit hook with language parity plan. Thanks folks. :thumbsup:
